target_customer: Builders', plumbing and timber merchants (UK style building suppliers) that extend trade credit to customers
problem: Merchants lose money when trade customers default and credit reports lag. Paperplane predicted defaults four or more weeks earlier using the merchant's own transaction data and sales rep knowledge.
business_model: B2B SaaS for credit risk management

founders.name: Daniel Kwak
education: Dropped out of a PhD in computational physics and ML (institution not listed)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page bio. Also led the seed round of Jack Hopkins' earlier startup.

founders.name: Jack Hopkins
education: University of Cambridge, postgraduate degree in Advanced Computer Science
previous_startups: Co-founded a company applying language models to API security (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Published research on generative language models per YC page.

founders.name: Ben Magolan
founders.background_notes: ML Ops tech lead at Xometry per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Default prediction from merchant transaction data requires ML and data integration with merchant systems, standard engineering with some hard modelling work.

defensibility.rationale: Models rely on each merchant's own data, which creates some lock in, but credit bureaus and credit control vendors could add similar scoring.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Paperplane.

market_need_then: Trade credit losses and late payments are a recurring pain for building suppliers, and the company claimed credit reports rely on lagging public data. No dated demand statistics were found.

branding.domain_note: Used paperplane.ai; other unrelated companies share the name Paperplane

brand_strength.rationale: No brand material found; an unrelated Indian healthtech company and other products share the name.

pivots.from: NLP for sales that updates Salesforce after sales calls (per the YC launch post referenced on the YC page)
pivots.to: Credit risk prediction for builders' merchants

outcome_analysis: Paperplane started with NLP for sales, moved to credit risk prediction for building merchants and is listed Inactive on the YC directory. Funding data show only a small amount from YC and angel style funds. No post mortem or press explains the end, so the cause of failure is not public.
